content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged brown bear frame. Host frame: the brown bear sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature that combines a european rhinoceros beetle and a brown bear. Head of the brown bear, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: brown bear body and legs, with its own dense fur everywhere else, plain coat, no stripes or spots; from the european rhinoceros beetle, as parts and materials on the brown bear's own body: a single curved horn of hard, glossy chitin rising from the brow; a covering of hard, glossy chitin plates with fine seams in its own colors that replaces the brown bear's fur over the back and flanks: it grows in the skin as the brown bear's own covering there, not as pieces added on top; the fur stops at the covering's edge, and the belly and legs keep the brown bear's own fur; the covering is a carapace grown in the skin like an armadillo's, shaped like a beetle's two elytra: one domed dorsal shield from the shoulders to the hips, in two halves meeting at a midline seam, never scattered plates. The covering follows the body outline. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs and visible breathing openings along the flanks. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration. Material reference: use @Image1 only for the material of the chitin plates: their color, surface texture and seams. Do not copy its body, head, legs or shape; the creature is the brown bear described above.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing hybrid bear beetle**
I'm planning a full-body, side three-quarter natural history illustration of a brown bear with chitin plates on its back and flanks, using the glossy deep brown material and seams from the reference, plus a single curved brow horn and flank breathing openings.
**Creating hybrid bear illustration**
I'm planning a natural history style side three-quarter view of a brown bear with a glossy reddish-brown chitin carapace from shoulders to hips, a curved forehead horn, and fur on the belly and legs, set against a plain light background.
**Refining hybrid bear beetle**
I'm preparing another generation to better integrate the chitin plates with the bear form, keeping the flank breathing openings while making the armor look more cohesive.
